subject: English
prompt: What is the main focus of the passage?
options: Why lithium-ion batteries have completely replaced supercapacitors
The operating mechanism, advantages, and primary trade-off of supercapacitors compared to batteries
How chemical reactions inside activated carbon destroy electrolytes
Why electric vehicles no longer require regenerative braking
explanation: The supplied compilation lists option B in its answer key. No worked solution is included in the PDF; this answer has not been certified by NUST.
context: Unlike conventional lithium-ion batteries, which store electrical energy chemically inside electrodes and therefore suffer from gradual capacity degradation over thousands of charge–discharge cycles, supercapacitors (electrochemical double-layer capacitors) store energy electrostatically at the interface between high-surface-area activated carbon electrodes and an electrolyte. Because no slow solid-state chemical reactions limit charge transfer, supercapacitors can absorb and deliver bursts of power within seconds and endure more than a million cycles with minimal wear. Their principal limitation remains lower specific energy density compared to batteries, prompting hybrid electric vehicle engineers to pair supercapacitors with battery packs to capture regenerative braking energy efficiently.
